Code Defect: When adding `<script>` or `<link>` tags that load resources from an external CDN (e.g., in `src/docs/index.html`), always include a Subresource Integrity (SRI) `integrity` attribute with the cryptographic hash of the resource, plus a matching `crossorigin` attribute. Loading CDN assets without an integrity check exposes users to supply-chain attacks.

In async rendering loops in diagram-dispatching code (e.g., `mermaid.ts`), do not use `Promise.all` for parallel `render` calls. Diagram database modules (e.g., `flowDb.js`) rely on module-level mutable state, so concurrent renders corrupt each other's output. Sequential `await` is required. This is a known architectural limitation tracked in issue #3577.

When documentation code examples reference mermaid via CDN, always include an explicit version pin. In source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` processed by the `docs.mts` build transform, use the `<MERMAID_VERSION>` placeholder. In files served directly (e.g., standalone HTML in `vdocs/`), hardcode the current major version (e.g., `@9`). Unversioned CDN URLs break archived docs when a new major version is released.

When adding or reviewing code examples in documentation that reference mermaid module file paths, verify filenames are correctly spelled — e.g., the ESM build artifact is `mermaid.esm.mjs`, not `mermaid.ems.mjs`.

When modifying header-generation logic in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts`, verify that the relative path in the autogenerated 'DO NOT EDIT' source-file link is derived from the *output* file's directory depth under `docs/`, not from the source file path. Spot-check generated headers for at least one top-level file and one subdirectory file.

Pre-release version identifiers in semver strings must include a dot before the numeric component (e.g., `9.2.1-rc.1`, not `9.2.1-rc1`). Without the dot, identifiers are compared lexicographically, causing `rc10 < rc9`. Verify this format whenever `package.json` version fields are modified.

When refactoring a callback from a function parameter into an optional interface property, verify that at least one concrete implementation actually sets that property before adding a conditional guard in the calling code. If no implementation sets it, remove the branch rather than leaving dead code.

When adding or modifying entries in the redirect map (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/redirect.ts`), verify that every non-empty target path resolves to an actual, content-bearing documentation page; spot-check target URLs in the running dev server before merging.

Use `window.location.replace()` instead of assigning to `window.location.href` when performing client-side redirects, so the source URL is not pushed onto the browser history stack and users can navigate back without being caught in a redirect loop.

In every diagram detector file (`*Detector.ts`) and diagram definition file (`*Diagram.ts` / `*Diagram-v*.ts`), exported constants must carry explicit type annotations (`const detector: DiagramDetector = …` and `export const diagram: DiagramDefinition = { … }`). Omitting these forfeits TypeScript's structural checking for required fields (e.g., `parser`, `db`, `renderer`, `styles`) and breaks consistency with the rest of the codebase.

When reviewing or adding parameterized test cases in diagram-detection tests (e.g., `diagram-orchestration.spec.ts`), verify that each `(input text, expected diagram type)` pair matches the actual detector logic. The mapping from input text to type name (e.g., `flowchart` vs `flowchart-v2`) is non-obvious — cross-check against the detector source code rather than assuming from the diagram keyword.

In a `"type": "module"` package, do not add `"main"` or `"require"` export fields pointing to `.js` files alongside ESM files — Node.js treats all `.js` files in that context as ESM, so `require()` will fail at runtime. If CJS support is needed, use `.cjs` extensions or place CJS files in a subdirectory with its own `{ "type": "commonjs" }` package.json.

When modifying `exports`, `types`, or `main` fields in package.json, verify that type exports are correct for all relevant `moduleResolution` modes using https://arethetypeswrong.github.io before merging, to catch CJS/ESM TypeScript incompatibilities (e.g., broken types under `moduleResolution: node16`).

When removing or renaming files in the `dist/` directory of a published npm package, check whether those paths are referenced by CDN URLs. `unpkg.com` returns a 404 for missing files (unlike jsdelivr, which falls back to older versions), permanently breaking downstream `<script src>` CDN links. The `dist/mermaid.min.js` filename in particular has a large number of CDN dependents and must be treated as a stable public artifact.

When bumping the `packageManager` version in `package.json` (this project uses pnpm), delete the lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`) entirely and regenerate it by running the new package manager's install command from scratch. Simply committing a manually edited lockfile does not guarantee stale entries from the prior version are fully removed.

When implementing runtime detection of a browser built-in API (e.g., `if (Intl.Segmenter)`), add unit tests that stub the API as `undefined` via `vi.stubGlobal` to exercise the fallback code path. In the test description or a comment, note which browser lacks support and link to the relevant bug report or spec discussion.

Mermaid diagram syntax changes must not break previously-valid diagram source. When modifying grammar productions (e.g., in `flow.jison`): (1) add regression tests for edge cases that were previously valid (e.g., trailing backslash in quoted labels, special characters at string boundaries), (2) when widening a non-terminal (e.g., replacing `alphaNum` with `idString`), add tests confirming newly-accepted forms and asserting previously-rejected forms still fail, (3) for reserved-keyword changes in identifiers, test keywords as prefixes, suffixes, and infixes with each permitted punctuation separator. When a conflict arises between a new feature and backward compatibility, the old behavior must be preserved.

When a TypeScript function accepts a destructured config/options parameter that callers may partially specify, assign defaults at the property level (e.g., `{ depth = 2, clobber = false }`) and mark those properties optional in the type. A whole-object default (`= {}`) only applies when the argument is entirely omitted — it does not merge missing fields from a partially-provided object. Do not combine destructuring defaults with `Object.assign` for the same parameter; choose one approach, preferring destructuring defaults.

In development demo files (e.g., under `demos/`) and client-side event-driven code (EventSource, WebSocket, etc.), ensure error event handlers explicitly log the error to the console rather than silently ignoring it, so failures are visible during development.

When configuring file-watcher ignore patterns (e.g., chokidar's `ignored` option), verify that patterns intended to exclude directories like `node_modules` match at all nesting levels (e.g., use `**/node_modules/**` glob syntax), not only at the root of the watched tree.

When defining TypeScript interfaces for diagram data objects (e.g., in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/commonTypes.ts`), audit actual call sites to determine which fields are genuinely optional before adding `?`. Do not mark all fields optional just to suppress TypeScript errors — only fields that are truly nullable or omittable at every call site should carry `?`; fields that are always required must remain non-optional to preserve type-safety guarantees.

When a JS-to-TS conversion includes any change that could alter runtime behavior (even a small bug fix such as correcting `x !== 'undefined'` to `x !== undefined`), run the project's end-to-end tests (`pnpm run e2e`) against the branch, comparing outputs against a `develop` baseline, before merging — to confirm that no diagram rendering outputs change unexpectedly.

When measuring elapsed or wall-clock duration (e.g., timing build steps or async operations), prefer `console.time()`/`console.timeEnd()` or `performance.now()` over `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` reflects the system wall clock and is not monotonic, making it unsuitable for measuring time intervals.
Maintainability and Readability: When destructuring but discarding one of the destructured variables (e.g., using `Object.entries` when only the value is needed), prefer an alternative that avoids unused variables (e.g., `Object.values`) to prevent `no-unused-vars` lint warnings.

When adding ESLint `overrides` in `.eslintrc.json` to suppress rules for test/spec files (e.g., `*.spec.{ts,js}`, `cypress/**`, `docs/**` globs), prefer setting rules to `"warn"` rather than `"off"` so newly introduced violations still appear in PR diffs; only use `"off"` when accumulated warning count is large enough to obscure real errors.

CI status badges in README files (`README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/README.md`, and other variants) must link to the currently active CI system (GitHub Actions). When updating any one README, check that all sibling README variants receive the same badge update.

Variables in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts` that hold a specific semver component must be named to reflect which component they contain (e.g., `MERMAID_MAJOR_VERSION` for just the major version, not a generic `mermaidVersion`).

When deprecating or removing public-facing config options, API methods, or package exports, document the change in the CHANGELOG or release notes — not only via in-code deprecation warnings — so existing consumers have clear migration guidance.

When a feature, config key, or code path is removed, replaced, or refactored, audit all related JSDoc blocks, inline comments, and log messages and remove or update any references to the old feature or prior logic; stale documentation and misleading log messages confuse future contributors.

When adding routing or navigation behavior inside the VitePress theme's `enhanceApp` hook (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`), prefer using VitePress's official router API (e.g., the `router` object from the `ctx` argument) over directly patching router lifecycle callbacks.

When adding non-obvious logic, workarounds, or hacks in build configuration files or plugin utilities (e.g., a dynamically constructed RegExp in `.vite/build.ts`, a workaround for an upstream bug), include inline comments that (1) explain in plain language what the code does and why the workaround is necessary, (2) attribute any external pattern or source it was adapted from (e.g., `// Adapted from the RegEx used by rollup-plugin-node`), and (3) link to the relevant issue, PR discussion, or upstream bug report so future maintainers can revisit it.

When a change involves both a mechanical file-format migration (e.g., converting a config from JSON to CJS/ESM, renaming files, restructuring without behavior changes) and substantive content changes, split them into separate commits so reviewers can clearly identify what actually changed in each step.

When reorganizing README layout (e.g., adding a centered logo/header), adopt a consistent strategy for badge placement rather than splitting badges across header and body without an explicit reason. Ensure quick-access navigation links (CDN, docs, contribution guide) remain visible and prominent; if relocated, they must reappear somewhere equally discoverable.

Before including links to project files (changelogs, migration guides, other docs) in prominent README sections, verify that the target files are actively maintained and up to date. Remove or replace links to stale or abandoned files to avoid misleading users.

Exported functions whose behavior depends on non-obvious constraints — such as argument ordering (e.g., `registerLazyLoadedDiagrams` where the first matching detector wins) or concurrency semantics (e.g., an execution queue that serializes concurrent calls) — must document these constraints explicitly in a TSDoc `@remarks` block so callers understand the implications.

When a function's signature changes (e.g., parameters added, removed, or retyped; callback-based to promise-based), update all JSDoc for that function: remove or rewrite stale `@param` entries, add `@param` tags for any undocumented parameters, and update inline code examples so they compile and run against the new API. Every parameter in the signature must have a corresponding `@param` tag.

Auto-generated files (e.g., those emitted by `unplugin-vue-components`, build pipelines, or code-generation scripts such as the contributors JSON) must be added to `.gitignore` and, where appropriate, also to `.prettierignore` and `cSpell.json` `ignorePaths`, so they are excluded from version control, formatting, and spell-checking.

When adding or modifying scripts (e.g., under `scripts/` or `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/scripts/`), use `ts-node-esm` — the project's established TypeScript script runner — rather than introducing alternatives like `esno` or `tsx`, to keep script execution consistent.

Prefer Node.js built-in `node:fs/promises` APIs over third-party filesystem utilities (such as `fs-extra`) when they offer equivalent functionality; for example, use `mkdir(path, { recursive: true })` instead of `fs-extra`'s `ensureDir` to avoid unnecessary dependencies.

All exported functions must have at least a basic TSDoc/JSDoc comment. When refactoring files (e.g., converting .js to .ts), verify that existing JSDoc comments on exported functions have not been accidentally removed in the process.

When calling APIs whose output depends on environment-specific defaults (e.g., `new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, ...)` using the host locale), add a code comment noting that output may vary across environments or default locales, and cite the relevant spec rationale if locale/platform sensitivity is non-obvious.

When defining a function type alias (or callback type) whose return value is a boolean predicate, include a TSDoc comment that explicitly states which boolean value represents the positive/success case (e.g., `/** Returns true if the line fits the constraint */`).

When modifying `flow.jison` or its companion JS modules, remove any grammar productions, token definitions, and token-list rules (e.g., orphaned `graphCodeTokens`, unused `alphaNumStatement`) that are no longer referenced by any other production, and delete corresponding dead helper code in the associated JS files. Verify with a grep or jison linting pass that no symbol is defined but unused.

When grammar changes affect which escape sequences or special characters are valid inside node or edge labels, update both `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/flowchart.md` and `docs/syntax/flowchart.md` to accurately reflect the current grammar: remove examples that no longer work, do not introduce examples for forms that have not been verified, and keep the two copies consistent with each other.

In `flow.jison`, keep shape-start/shape-end lexer token rules (e.g., `STADIUMSTART`, `SUBROUTINESTART`, `CYLINDERSTART`) decoupled from text-content state management. Handle quoted and unquoted text within the `text` grammar production (or a dedicated `string` production) rather than embedding `pushState`/`popState` calls inside the lexer rules that emit shape-start tokens. Mixing these concerns produces lexer rules whose entry state does not match their intended exit condition.

In sandbox-aware SVG selection utilities (e.g., `rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts`), scope intermediate variables like `sandboxElement` and `doc` inside the `if (securityLevel === 'sandbox')` branch rather than hoisting them to the outer scope. When designing such utilities, evaluate whether callers genuinely need the intermediate `Document` or root node — if a renderer misuses `doc` for operations that should target the SVG element, fix the renderer rather than expanding the utility's return type.

Retain a `log.debug(...)` call at the top of diagram renderer `draw` functions even when the function body is not wrapped in a try/catch; it serves as a diagnostic breadcrumb confirming that rendering was entered and helps narrow down where a silent failure occurred.

When exporting a diagram definition object from a diagram module, prefer `export default diagram` over a named `export const diagram` to avoid forcing every import site to alias (e.g., `{ diagram as errorDiagram }`). If a named export is required, name the constant after the diagram (e.g., `export const errorDiagram`) so that imports can consume it without aliasing.

When reviewing `package.json` changes, verify that no deprecated packages have been introduced — including ones that appear to have been auto-added or re-sorted by the package manager (e.g., pnpm) rather than explicitly by the author — and remove any packages flagged as deprecated.

In TypeScript tooling files (e.g., under `.esbuild/`), add explicit type annotations to non-trivial local variables unless their type is already fully and unambiguously constrained by a strongly-typed API; do not rely on implicit inference when the variable's shape is not immediately obvious.

When a JS-to-TS migration reveals a runtime bug (e.g., a comparison against the string `'undefined'` that should instead check the value `undefined`), explicitly call it out in the PR description as a bug fix rather than treating it as an incidental refactoring detail. This helps reviewers understand the behavioral scope of the change and decide whether additional testing or a separate fix PR is warranted.
Performance Issue: When reviewing changes to build entry points in `.esbuild/util.cjs` (or any esbuild build configuration), verify that each new entry point is intentional and explicitly justified: each additional entry point produces a full separate bundle in `dist/`, potentially adding tens of megabytes to the output.
Code Style: Proofread prose in JSDoc comments, documentation, log messages, and thrown error strings for spelling and grammar errors. These appear in production output and developer tooling, making typos (e.g., 'Remozing' instead of 'Removing', 'In one is provided' → 'If one is provided') harder to catch than code mistakes.
In GitHub Actions workflow YAML files, when a step needs to execute from a specific directory, use the `working-directory` step attribute rather than embedding a `cd` command inside the `run:` block.

In test files, template-literal diagram strings should not include a trailing newline before the closing backtick. The backtick should appear immediately after the last content line, and new tests should match the formatting convention established in the same test file.
TypeScript `interface` declarations should end with a trailing semicolon after the closing brace (`};`), for consistency with `type` alias declarations in the same file.

Do not leave commented-out code, dead code, or unresolved inline comments whose purpose is pending verification (e.g., 'check with X before removing') in a merge request. Delete dead and commented-out code entirely (in both source and test files), and resolve pending-verification comments — either remove them or convert to proper TSDoc — before merging. Git history preserves prior versions.

In jison grammar rule actions, prefer named semantic-value aliases (`$symbolName` or explicit label aliases via `symbol[alias]` syntax) over positional `$1`/`$2` references. Named aliases prevent off-by-one errors when alternatives are reordered or new tokens are inserted, and make the rule body self-documenting.

When flowchart parser tests exercise the same assertion body across multiple shapes, edge types, or token categories, use `it.each` or a plain JS array iteration (`forEach`/`map` over a data-table) rather than duplicating the test body for each case. This reduces file size, makes coverage intent explicit, and makes adding new cases trivial.

When adding or reordering numbered step headings (e.g., `#### N. Title`) in documentation, verify that step numbers are strictly sequential with no duplicates — each new section must use the next unused number.
In TypeScript files, use type-only import declarations (`import type { Foo } from '...'`) rather than inline type qualifiers inside a mixed import list (`import { type Foo } from '...'`).

`packages/mermaid/src/config.type.ts` is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` and must not be modified manually. New diagram configuration types must be added to the YAML schema file and the TypeScript file regenerated via the project's build script.

New diagram jison grammars must not include `%%{...}%%` directive parsing logic; directives are pre-processed by the framework before any diagram-specific grammar runs, making diagram-level directive rules redundant and potentially conflicting.

Grammar rules for bracket-delimited lists (e.g., `[ item, item, ... ]`) should use explicit bracket terminals and a dedicated non-terminal for the list body; avoid recursive rules that allow unbalanced constructions such as `[ 10 [ 20 ]`.

In jison lexers, use `pushState` instead of `begin` for delimiter nesting, and ensure every `pushState` on an opening delimiter has a matching `popState` on the corresponding closing delimiter; avoid creating unnecessary intermediate states when the state stack already manages nesting. Using `begin` replaces (rather than pushes) the current state, which can corrupt the state stack.
In jison lexer rules, list closing delimiter tokens (e.g., `"]"`) before content-matching patterns within the same lexer state so they take higher matching priority and cannot be consumed as content.

When `accTitle` and `accDescr` accessibility tokens appear in a jison grammar (even if copied from another diagram), they must be fully implemented with corresponding grammar actions and DB calls; leaving them as stubs breaks screen-reader accessibility for the diagram.

When copying regex patterns into a new jison grammar from an existing diagram, review each pattern for correctness in the new context; copied patterns (e.g., for directive comment detection or negative lookaheads) may only partially work and should be understood before being retained.

DOM elements created for text dimension measurement (e.g., hidden `<text>` nodes appended to SVG) must be removed after use to avoid polluting the document; prefer existing project utilities such as `computeWidthOfText` or `computeDimensionOfText` in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/createText.ts` that already handle cleanup.

When copying or merging nested config or theme objects, use the project's `cleanAndMerge` utility or `structuredClone` rather than shallow spread operators (`{ ...obj }`); shallow spread does not deep-copy nested objects and can produce silent shared-reference mutations.

Diagram detector regexes must require the complete diagram keyword including any suffix as declared in the grammar (e.g., `/^\s*xychart-beta/` for a diagram declared as `xychart-beta`); omitting the suffix silently pre-empts the project's explicit beta-to-stable graduation process. Detector regexes should also be case-sensitive, consistent with other diagram detectors in the project.

When a class method's output depends on other mutable state (e.g., `setAxisPosition` affects the coordinate range), updating that state should automatically trigger any dependent recalculation inside the same method; callers should not be required to invoke methods in a specific order to get correct results.

When reviewing typo-fix changes, check whether any corrected string literal is part of the library's externally observable API — for example, error message text that is thrown or returned to callers who may be matching it programmatically. Changing such strings is a breaking change; flag it for rejection or deferral to the next major release rather than treating it as a safe cosmetic fix.

Diagram text preprocessing (such as entity encoding) must be applied exactly once, in the `Diagram` class constructor (`packages/mermaid/src/Diagram.ts`), rather than in downstream rendering or API functions like `mermaidAPI.render`. Centralizing the transformation at construction time prevents double-encoding bugs and removes the need for callers to remember to pre-process text before passing it to the API.

Avoid polynomial (potentially catastrophic-backtracking) regular expressions on uncontrolled user input. Patterns that combine multiple greedy quantifiers with overlapping character classes — such as `style.*:\S*#.*;` — can degrade to exponential time on crafted inputs, creating a ReDoS vulnerability. Use more precise, non-backtracking patterns (e.g., negated character classes or possessive quantifiers) when processing diagram text, and flag any such patterns for a security review.

When configuring the Shiki syntax-highlighting theme in the VitePress config (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/config.ts`), always use the dual-mode object form `{ light: '<light-theme>', dark: '<dark-theme>' }` instead of a single theme string. A single string will break code-block highlighting in whichever color mode it was not chosen for, since the site supports both light and dark modes.

When using DOMPurify hooks in `common.ts` `removeScript()`, register *all* hooks—including `afterSanitizeAttributes`—before calling `DOMPurify.sanitize()`, not after; and remove each hook afterward with `DOMPurify.removeHook()` to prevent hooks from accumulating across repeated calls.

When re-applying an HTML attribute that DOMPurify strips (e.g., `target` on `<a>` elements), restore the attribute's exact original value rather than substituting a hardcoded default; only add security-hardening companion attributes (e.g., `rel="noopener noreferrer"`) for the specific values that require them (e.g., `target="_blank"`).

Before adding calls to DOMPurify hook methods such as `addHook` in `common.ts`, verify that those methods are available in the Jest test environment; if DOMPurify is mocked or only partially shimmed in tests, extend the mock (or use a real DOM environment like jsdom) so that the full hook API is exercisable.

When simplifying DOM positioning arithmetic that mixes DOMRect properties (e.g., `rect.top`, `rect.bottom`), scroll offsets (`window.scrollY`, `document.body.scrollTop`), and numeric constants, verify that the simplified expression is mathematically equivalent under all scroll states and document the reasoning — either in an inline comment or the PR description — so reviewers can confirm correctness.

In `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml`, use `type: number` for configuration properties that can accept floating-point values; use `type: integer` only when the property semantically requires a whole number (e.g., a count that is always integral). Using `integer` for float-capable properties will cause schema validation to reject valid values.
Maintainability and Readability: When destructuring but discarding one of the destructured variables (e.g., using `Object.entries` when only the value is needed), prefer an alternative that avoids unused variables (e.g., `Object.values`) to prevent `no-unused-vars` lint warnings.

When adding ESLint `overrides` in `.eslintrc.json` to suppress rules for test/spec files (e.g., `*.spec.{ts,js}`, `cypress/**`, `docs/**` globs), prefer setting rules to `"warn"` rather than `"off"` so newly introduced violations still appear in PR diffs; only use `"off"` when accumulated warning count is large enough to obscure real errors.

CI status badges in README files (`README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/README.md`, and other variants) must link to the currently active CI system (GitHub Actions). When updating any one README, check that all sibling README variants receive the same badge update.

Variables in `packages/mermaid/src/docs.mts` that hold a specific semver component must be named to reflect which component they contain (e.g., `MERMAID_MAJOR_VERSION` for just the major version, not a generic `mermaidVersion`).

When deprecating or removing public-facing config options, API methods, or package exports, document the change in the CHANGELOG or release notes — not only via in-code deprecation warnings — so existing consumers have clear migration guidance.

When a feature, config key, or code path is removed, replaced, or refactored, audit all related JSDoc blocks, inline comments, and log messages and remove or update any references to the old feature or prior logic; stale documentation and misleading log messages confuse future contributors.

When adding routing or navigation behavior inside the VitePress theme's `enhanceApp` hook (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`), prefer using VitePress's official router API (e.g., the `router` object from the `ctx` argument) over directly patching router lifecycle callbacks.

When adding non-obvious logic, workarounds, or hacks in build configuration files or plugin utilities (e.g., a dynamically constructed RegExp in `.vite/build.ts`, a workaround for an upstream bug), include inline comments that (1) explain in plain language what the code does and why the workaround is necessary, (2) attribute any external pattern or source it was adapted from (e.g., `// Adapted from the RegEx used by rollup-plugin-node`), and (3) link to the relevant issue, PR discussion, or upstream bug report so future maintainers can revisit it.

When a change involves both a mechanical file-format migration (e.g., converting a config from JSON to CJS/ESM, renaming files, restructuring without behavior changes) and substantive content changes, split them into separate commits so reviewers can clearly identify what actually changed in each step.

When reorganizing README layout (e.g., adding a centered logo/header), adopt a consistent strategy for badge placement rather than splitting badges across header and body without an explicit reason. Ensure quick-access navigation links (CDN, docs, contribution guide) remain visible and prominent; if relocated, they must reappear somewhere equally discoverable.

Before including links to project files (changelogs, migration guides, other docs) in prominent README sections, verify that the target files are actively maintained and up to date. Remove or replace links to stale or abandoned files to avoid misleading users.

Exported functions whose behavior depends on non-obvious constraints — such as argument ordering (e.g., `registerLazyLoadedDiagrams` where the first matching detector wins) or concurrency semantics (e.g., an execution queue that serializes concurrent calls) — must document these constraints explicitly in a TSDoc `@remarks` block so callers understand the implications.

When a function's signature changes (e.g., parameters added, removed, or retyped; callback-based to promise-based), update all JSDoc for that function: remove or rewrite stale `@param` entries, add `@param` tags for any undocumented parameters, and update inline code examples so they compile and run against the new API. Every parameter in the signature must have a corresponding `@param` tag.

Auto-generated files (e.g., those emitted by `unplugin-vue-components`, build pipelines, or code-generation scripts such as the contributors JSON) must be added to `.gitignore` and, where appropriate, also to `.prettierignore` and `cSpell.json` `ignorePaths`, so they are excluded from version control, formatting, and spell-checking.

When adding or modifying scripts (e.g., under `scripts/` or `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/scripts/`), use `ts-node-esm` — the project's established TypeScript script runner — rather than introducing alternatives like `esno` or `tsx`, to keep script execution consistent.

Prefer Node.js built-in `node:fs/promises` APIs over third-party filesystem utilities (such as `fs-extra`) when they offer equivalent functionality; for example, use `mkdir(path, { recursive: true })` instead of `fs-extra`'s `ensureDir` to avoid unnecessary dependencies.

All exported functions must have at least a basic TSDoc/JSDoc comment. When refactoring files (e.g., converting .js to .ts), verify that existing JSDoc comments on exported functions have not been accidentally removed in the process.

When calling APIs whose output depends on environment-specific defaults (e.g., `new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, ...)` using the host locale), add a code comment noting that output may vary across environments or default locales, and cite the relevant spec rationale if locale/platform sensitivity is non-obvious.

When defining a function type alias (or callback type) whose return value is a boolean predicate, include a TSDoc comment that explicitly states which boolean value represents the positive/success case (e.g., `/** Returns true if the line fits the constraint */`).

When modifying or creating jison grammars (e.g., `flow.jison` or new diagram grammars), remove any grammar productions, token definitions, token-list rules, and lexer states that are no longer referenced by any other production, and delete corresponding dead helper code in the associated JS files. When creating a new grammar by adapting an existing one, audit and remove all carried-over rules that are not actually used. Verify with a grep or jison linting pass that no symbol is defined but unused.

When grammar changes affect which escape sequences or special characters are valid inside node or edge labels, update both `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/flowchart.md` and `docs/syntax/flowchart.md` to accurately reflect the current grammar: remove examples that no longer work, do not introduce examples for forms that have not been verified, and keep the two copies consistent with each other.

In `flow.jison`, keep shape-start/shape-end lexer token rules (e.g., `STADIUMSTART`, `SUBROUTINESTART`, `CYLINDERSTART`) decoupled from text-content state management. Handle quoted and unquoted text within the `text` grammar production (or a dedicated `string` production) rather than embedding `pushState`/`popState` calls inside the lexer rules that emit shape-start tokens. Mixing these concerns produces lexer rules whose entry state does not match their intended exit condition.

In sandbox-aware SVG selection utilities (e.g., `rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts`), scope intermediate variables like `sandboxElement` and `doc` inside the `if (securityLevel === 'sandbox')` branch rather than hoisting them to the outer scope. When designing such utilities, evaluate whether callers genuinely need the intermediate `Document` or root node — if a renderer misuses `doc` for operations that should target the SVG element, fix the renderer rather than expanding the utility's return type.

Retain a `log.debug(...)` call at the top of diagram renderer `draw` functions even when the function body is not wrapped in a try/catch; it serves as a diagnostic breadcrumb confirming that rendering was entered and helps narrow down where a silent failure occurred.

When exporting a diagram definition object from a diagram module, prefer `export default diagram` over a named `export const diagram` to avoid forcing every import site to alias (e.g., `{ diagram as errorDiagram }`). If a named export is required, name the constant after the diagram (e.g., `export const errorDiagram`) so that imports can consume it without aliasing.

When reviewing `package.json` changes, verify that no deprecated packages have been introduced — including ones that appear to have been auto-added or re-sorted by the package manager (e.g., pnpm) rather than explicitly by the author — and remove any packages flagged as deprecated.

In TypeScript tooling files (e.g., under `.esbuild/`), add explicit type annotations to non-trivial local variables unless their type is already fully and unambiguously constrained by a strongly-typed API; do not rely on implicit inference when the variable's shape is not immediately obvious.

When a JS-to-TS migration reveals a runtime bug (e.g., a comparison against the string `'undefined'` that should instead check the value `undefined`), explicitly call it out in the PR description as a bug fix rather than treating it as an incidental refactoring detail. This helps reviewers understand the behavioral scope of the change and decide whether additional testing or a separate fix PR is warranted.

When adding or updating branch-based Live Editor preview environments, use the `<branch>.git.mermaid.live` subdomain naming convention (not names like `beta.mermaid.live` that imply npm pre-release status). In documentation referencing these previews, use wording that clearly conveys unreleased status (e.g., 'git `develop` branch preview'). Build scripts (e.g., `scripts/editor.bash`) should append the short git commit hash to the mermaid package version so users can identify which commit a preview was built from.

Complex token patterns such as comma-separated lists or structured data should be expressed as non-terminal grammar rules in jison rather than as single large regexes in the lexer; grammar rules produce better parse error messages and are easier to maintain.

When multiple grammar rules (e.g., for different plot types or diagram variants) parse structurally identical data, unify them into a single shared non-terminal; duplication leads to divergent behavior and maintenance overhead.

Default values for new diagram configuration options must be defined in `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml` (following the instructions in the file header), not hardcoded in the diagram's DB module; the schema is the single source of truth for defaults.

In diagram DB modules, all module-level mutable state variables should be grouped at the top of the file (or collected in a single reset object) so that the `clear()` function can reset all state in one place; variables scattered throughout the file are easily missed when adding a reset.
Parser test specifications (`*.jison.spec.ts` files) must include test cases for invalid or malformed inputs that are expected to fail to parse, not only valid happy-path inputs.

Diagram renderers should use the `selectSvgElement` utility from `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts` for obtaining a typed SVG element reference rather than reimplementing that selection inline.
Each section in demo HTML files under `demos/` should have a unique, descriptive heading; avoid repeating the same `<h1>` text for multiple diagram variants in the same file.

When theme variables for a new diagram are structured as a nested object in `themeVariables` (e.g., `themeVariables.xyChart.titleColor`), keep the structure consistent with how other diagrams in the project expose their theme variables to avoid introducing an inconsistent API surface.

Do not add diagram-specific methods (e.g., methods that only certain diagram types expose, such as `getMessages` or `getActors`) to the shared `DiagramDB` interface in `packages/mermaid/src/diagram-api/types.ts`. Diagram-specific DB methods must be typed in the individual diagram's own type definitions, keeping the common interface limited to methods every diagram implementation actually shares.

When extracting cohesive utility functions from a large module (e.g., moving `encodeEntities`/`decodeEntities` out of `mermaidAPI.ts`), prefer creating a dedicated, focused module (e.g., `entities.ts`) rather than appending them to the general-purpose `utils.ts`. This prevents `utils.ts` from growing into an unrelated grab-bag and makes the utilities easier to discover and test in isolation.

Whenever sanitization behavior in `common.ts` is changed, add unit tests in `common.spec.ts` covering each meaningful input variant: attribute absent, attribute set to a safe/benign value, and attribute set to a risky value that triggers additional hardening.

When generating IDs for diagram edges, use a lexically meaningful template that embeds the source and target node identifiers along with a disambiguating counter—e.g., `id_${edge.id1}_${edge.id2}_${cnt}`—rather than building an opaque ID from a bare counter alone.

When copying a method or code block from a sibling class or module (e.g., a different axis class, a different diagram type), immediately rename all internal identifiers, string literals, and `groupTexts` values to match the new context. Copy-paste identifier mismatches (e.g., `'bottom-axis'` in a top-axis class, or a method name referencing the wrong axis) are a frequent source of silent bugs.
Contributors should not self-resolve review conversation threads after addressing feedback; leave threads open so the reviewer can verify the fix and close them during re-review.

Each `it` test block should cover a single concern; if a test body manually calls `clearMocks()` when a `beforeEach` hook already handles clearing, that is a sign the test should be split into independent `it` blocks.

When documenting a feature that supports multiple modes, orientations, or options, begin the section with an introductory summary listing all supported modes (including syntax keywords and which is the default), then describe the concrete visual behavior of each mode explicitly — state how primary elements flow directionally and how structural elements are arranged — rather than relying on abstract labels alone.
Performance Issue: When reviewing changes to build entry points in `.esbuild/util.cjs` (or any esbuild build configuration), verify that each new entry point is intentional and explicitly justified: each additional entry point produces a full separate bundle in `dist/`, potentially adding tens of megabytes to the output.
Code Style: Proofread prose in JSDoc comments, documentation, log messages, thrown error strings, test fixtures, and demo files for spelling, grammar, and terminological accuracy. These appear in production output, developer tooling, or snapshot diffs, making errors harder to catch than code mistakes. In documentation under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`, verify that descriptions match what the grammar actually supports (e.g., 'single word' vs 'single line' when describing quoting rules).
In GitHub Actions workflow YAML files, when a step needs to execute from a specific directory, use the `working-directory` step attribute rather than embedding a `cd` command inside the `run:` block.

In test files, template-literal diagram strings should not include a trailing newline before the closing backtick. The backtick should appear immediately after the last content line, and new tests should match the formatting convention established in the same test file.
TypeScript `interface` declarations should end with a trailing semicolon after the closing brace (`};`), for consistency with `type` alias declarations in the same file.

Do not leave commented-out code, dead code, or unresolved inline comments whose purpose is pending verification (e.g., 'check with X before removing') in a merge request. Delete dead and commented-out code entirely (in both source and test files), and resolve pending-verification comments — either remove them or convert to proper TSDoc — before merging. Git history preserves prior versions.

In jison grammar rule actions, prefer named semantic-value aliases (`$symbolName` or explicit label aliases via `symbol[alias]` syntax) over positional `$1`/`$2` references. Named aliases prevent off-by-one errors when alternatives are reordered or new tokens are inserted, and make the rule body self-documenting.

When flowchart parser tests exercise the same assertion body across multiple shapes, edge types, or token categories, use `it.each` or a plain JS array iteration (`forEach`/`map` over a data-table) rather than duplicating the test body for each case. This reduces file size, makes coverage intent explicit, and makes adding new cases trivial.

When adding or reordering numbered step headings (e.g., `#### N. Title`) in documentation, verify that step numbers are strictly sequential with no duplicates — each new section must use the next unused number.
In TypeScript files, use type-only import declarations (`import type { Foo } from '...'`) rather than inline type qualifiers inside a mixed import list (`import { type Foo } from '...'`).

In jison lexers, whitespace should be ignored in the INITIAL state (e.g., a rule that consumes `\s+` with no action) rather than returned as tokens and threaded through grammar rules; only include whitespace tokens in states where they carry semantic meaning.
Non-terminal names in jison grammars should not be prefixed with 'parse' (the whole file is a parser); ensure names are correctly spelled (e.g., `commaSeparated` not `commaSeprate`).

When the same regex pattern applies across multiple jison lexer states, combine the states in a single rule using a comma-separated state list (e.g., `<state1,state2>regexp { ... }`) rather than duplicating the rule once per state.

Inline numeric literals used as ratios, thresholds, or percentages in rendering calculations should be extracted to named constants at the top of the module (e.g., `const BAR_WIDTH_TO_TICK_WIDTH_RATIO = 0.7`).

Avoid `// @ts-ignore` for type narrowing; instead use explicit type casts (e.g., `diagObj.db as XYChartDB`). If a `// @ts-ignore` is genuinely unavoidable (e.g., a known gap in a third-party library's types such as Jison), replace the bare comment with a descriptive explanation of why the ignore is needed.
Diagram definition objects should omit optional properties that are not yet implemented (e.g., `styles`) rather than including them with empty arrays or undefined values.
TypeScript source files in this project use lowercase filenames (e.g., `interfaces.ts`, `baseAxis.ts`); do not use PascalCase filenames such as `Interfaces.ts` or `BaseAxis.ts`.
TypeScript interface names must not be prefixed with `I` (e.g., use `TextDimensionCalculator`, not `ITextDimensionCalculator`); the project does not follow the Hungarian `I`-prefix convention.
When an `if` block returns or throws early, remove the subsequent `else` block; it is structurally unnecessary and adds indentation noise.

In test fixtures, documentation, and demo files, prefer YAML frontmatter notation (`---
config:
  ...
---`) over `%%{init: ...}%%` directive syntax for configuring diagram examples; YAML frontmatter is the recommended approach for new grammars.
Remove unnecessary `log.trace` calls from diagram rendering code before merging; keep only meaningful diagnostic logs at `log.debug` level. Excessive trace logging adds noise in production builds.
Method and function names in TypeScript must fully spell out words without abbreviations or typos (e.g., `getDrawableElementsForBottomAxis`, not `getDrawableElemsForBottomAxes`).

In tests, prefer direct indexed assertions (`expect(array[0].property).toBe(...)`) over `.forEach()` loops when asserting on specific elements. Direct assertions produce more targeted failure messages and are easier to read as documentation of expected behavior.

When adding links to GitHub Issues in project documentation, consolidate open and closed issue searches into a single link using the `?q=is%3Aissue` query parameter (e.g., `https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues?q=is%3Aissue`) and label it to indicate it covers both states.
